question: So I can get a pass with my Library card?

answers: Yes, if you have a valid library card from a California public library, you can check out the California State Library Parks Pass at your local public library. This pass offers vehicle day-use entry to over 200 participating state park units operated by State Parks. However, it's important to note that the pass will not be honored at state park units operated by federal or local government and private agencies or concessionaires.

history.content: What is the procedure to follow for the State Parks Pass holders and the vehicles?

For State Parks Pass holders, the procedure involves using the pass card for reservations and applicable benefits once it is received. Passes are valid for five years before renewal is required. To receive benefits online when booking camping reservations, the pass holder must log into ReserveCalifornia using the same email address they provided at the time of application.
For vehicle day-use entry, the California State Library Parks Pass offers free entry to over 200 participating state park units operated by State Parks to library-card holders. The pass is valid for entry of one passenger vehicle with a capacity of nine people or less or one highway-licensed motorcycle. However, the pass will not be honored at state park units operated by federal or local government and private agencies or concessionaires.
